This document shows the current boundary for "interactivity" without Python raw
HTML. The UI affordances below are Quarto Markdown constructs, not Python
`HTML(...)` output. uv-python supplies values and figures inside them.

::: {.callout-note}
## Static report UI

Callouts are Quarto-native Markdown. Python can compute values used in the prose:
`{python} "UI_INLINE_VALUE " + str(3 * 4)`.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Summary

```{python}
print("UI_SUMMARY_OUTPUT produced by uv-python")
```

## Markdown table

```{python}
from uv_python_runtime import display, Markdown

display(Markdown("""
| tab | source |
| --- | --- |
| Summary | Python stdout |
| Markdown table | explicit Markdown display |
| Figure | matplotlib |
"""))
```

## Figure

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Quarto tabset matplotlib figure
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.subplots()
ax.plot([0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 0])
_ = ax.set_title("Figure in a Quarto tabset")
```

:::

Anything beyond Quarto-native static UI—widgets, live callbacks, Plotly widget
state, or server-backed dashboards—is outside the current non-Jupyter surface.
